headline: The Trump administration has dropped a request that US AI developers not give the British government early access to new models for safety testing, the Telegraph reports.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: a change in who may test the most advanced AI models before release, but it rests on one newspaper's report with no comment from the White House or the companies.
importance_line: British government testers can again check leading US models before the public sees them, which matters to anyone relying on those safety checks, but the report comes from one newspaper and Trump's spokespeople, OpenAI and Anthropic had not responded, so the exact scope of the change is unconfirmed.
source: The Telegraph, as relayed by Reuters
summary: The Telegraph reported on Sunday 11 Oct 2026, as relayed by Reuters, that the Trump administration has withdrawn an earlier request to AI developers, including OpenAI and Anthropic, to keep new models away from Britain's AI Security Institute (the government body that tests the most advanced models) until they are released. Reuters calls this a softer US stance on international AI safety work and notes that Trump's new AI task force on Friday told developers to report security incidents involving their models.
notes: Reuters page returned HTTP 401; the same Reuters text was read on The Hindu, and Startup Fortune was read for context (it says the pause began 24 Sep 2026 and lasted 17 days; single-source, left out). The Telegraph original was not opened, so the credit goes to the Telegraph as relayed by Reuters.
